messages:
alex_lee: FYI, customer reported that their refund request returned 200 but instead created an invoice adjustment. Escalating — looks like a function-call routed to the wrong tool.

mira_gomez: Ugh. Which tool was chosen by the router?

alex_lee: Router selected adjust_invoice instead of issue_refund. Payload from app: `{
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "adjust_invoice",
    "arguments": {
      "invoice_id": "inv_12345",
      "amount": "-50.00",
      "reason": "customer requested refund"
    }
  }
}`

jamal: Wait the amount was a string with a negative sign? That might be making the selector confused. Our schemas expect numeric amount for issue_refund but adjust_invoice allows string reason+amount?

ops-bot: model-router: selected_tool=adjust_invoice reason_score_delta=0.03 compatible_fields=[invoice_id, amount, reason] model_version=redwood/assistant-v1.4

alex_lee: Repro steps I ran on staging: 1) Send same tool call through API 2) observe router decision in trace 3) backend invoked adjust_invoice lambda and created invoice credit.

sophia_ng: Can you paste the function definitions the model sees? Even a trimmed view is fine.

alex_lee: Sure — simplified signatures: `issue_refund(invoice_id: string, amount: number, currency: string, reason: string)` and `adjust_invoice(invoice_id: string, amount: string, note: string)` — the model prefers adjust_invoice when amount is string and note/reason overlap.

mira_gomez: Ah, schema ambiguity. Two things: enforce types in the function-calling layer (coerce/validate amount as number) and add a discriminator field or enum like transaction_type.

jamal: Short-term mitigation: update router policy to prefer issue_refund when amount < 0 or when caller header x-request-intent=refund. Also validate and reject malformed args before invoking any tool.

alex_lee: I added a quick guard in staging: if amount is string try parseFloat and if numeric -> prefer issue_refund. Re-ran repro and it picks issue_refund now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled staging patch fea-guard-parse-amount -> success (runbook link: https://redwood.runbook/fea-guard-parse-amount) :thumbsup:

mira_gomez: Longer-term: update model-visible function schemas to use unambiguous field names (amount_cents: integer, operation: ["refund","adjustment"]) and tighten types. We'll also add an eval to catch similar misroutes.

alex_lee: Filed support escalation ticket with notes and repro + staging trace: INC-2025-783. Adding Amelia from payments to loop.

sophia_ng: Thanks. If we want to be extra safe, add a fallback check in the backend: if adjust_invoice was called but payload matches refund pattern, automatically call issue_refund and mark adjust_invoice as ignored, plus alert ops. Might be hairy but prevents customer-facing mistakes.

jamal: Agree on alerting. Let's implement strict validation and a warning metric for misroute_hits. Will follow up with a PR for schemas and a router policy change.

alex_lee: Great. For the ticket I included: raw request, staging trace, function signatures, ops logs, and recommended fixes (validation, discriminator, router policy). Leaving this thread open for any new findings. :ear:
